Buzek for the Parliament and E.
- [NDM-1, 2010](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/event/ndm-1-2010/): A study published online in August 2010 in The Lancet Infectious Diseases describing the spread of NDM-1 — New Delhi metallo-beta-lactamase-1, an enzyme that destroys carbapenems, the antibiotics kept for infections…
- [The 2020 shutdown](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/event/covid-shutdown-2020/): The year cross-border care stopped. On 11 March 2020 the Director-General of the World Health Organization told a media briefing in Geneva: "We have therefore made the assessment that COVID-19 can be characterized as a…
- [The Declaration of Istanbul, 2008](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/event/istanbul-declaration-2008/): A consensus statement agreed at an international summit in Istanbul in 2008, convened by The Transplantation Society and the International Society of Nephrology, which defined organ trafficking, transplant commercialism…
- [The Dominican mycobacterial outbreaks, 2013–14 and 2017](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/event/dominican-republic-ntm-outbreak/): Two multi-state clusters of rapidly growing nontuberculous mycobacteria — environmental bacteria that infect surgical wounds and take months of antibiotics to clear — in United States residents who had cosmetic surgery…
- [The IMTJ Medical Travel Summit and Awards](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/event/imtj-summit/): The trade's own annual gathering, run by the publisher of the International Medical Travel Journal alongside an awards ceremony.
- [The Matamoros fungal meningitis outbreak, 2023](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/event/mexico-fungal-meningitis-2023/): An outbreak of fungal meningitis among people — almost all of them residents of the United States — who had procedures under epidural anaesthesia at two clinics in Matamoros, Tamaulipas, in the first five months of…
- [Türkiye's hair transplant boom](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/event/turkiye-hair-boom/): The growth of hair restoration surgery sold to foreign buyers in Türkiye, mostly in Istanbul, into the most visible single procedure in cross-border care.

## Words
- [ASA grade](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/word/asa-grade/): A six-point scale describing how well a patient is before an operation, from ASA I, healthy, to ASA VI, declared brain-dead with organs being removed for donation, with an E appended where the surgery is an emergency.
- [Bundled payment](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/word/bundled-payment/): One payment covering everything a patient needs for a defined episode — the admission, the surgeon, the rehabilitation, the readmission if it happens — across every provider involved, for a fixed number of days after…
- [Case rate](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/word/case-rate/): One flat amount for one case, agreed in advance. A trade description puts it at its bluntest: under a case rate "providers receive a flat reimbursement rate for every patient visit, no matter what service they provide".
- [Circumvention travel](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/word/circumvention-travel/): Travelling to a country where a treatment is lawful in order to have it, because it is prohibited at home. The treatment is legal where it happens.
- [Co-payment](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/word/co-payment/): A fixed sum the patient pays for a covered service while the payer pays the rest.
- [Cycle](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/word/cycle/): One round of stimulation, egg collection, fertilisation and transfer.
- [Day case](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/word/day-case/): Treatment that occupies a hospital bed for part of a day and no night.
- [DRG](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/word/drg/): A bucket. Every inpatient stay is sorted at discharge into one group by diagnosis, procedures and complications, each group carries a weight, and the weight times a base rate is what the hospital is paid — the same…
- [Facilitator](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/word/facilitator/): The commercial party between a patient and a hospital abroad. It gathers records, produces a quote, books the surgeon, often books the flight and the hotel, and meets the patient at the airport.
- [FUE](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/word/fue/): Harvesting hair by cutting individual follicular units out of the donor area one at a time through small circular punches, rather than taking a strip of scalp and dissecting it.
- [Graft](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/word/graft/): In the older surgical sense, tissue moved from one place to another and expected to take.
- [Health tourism](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/word/health-tourism/): The wider administrative category: travel for treatment, for a cure, for thermal and spa stays, and for the care of travellers who fall ill while abroad.
- [Informed consent](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/word/informed-consent/): A patient's agreement to a procedure, given after being told what it involves, what it risks and what the alternatives are.
- [Length of stay](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/word/length-of-stay/): How long a patient occupies a hospital bed. On a price page it is a number of nights the seller has budgeted for; in a health statistic it is a measured average across discharges.
- [Medical tourism](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/word/medical-tourism/): The most widely used name for travelling to another country to be treated, and the most argued-about. This site writes medical travel and cross-border care instead.
- [Medical travel](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/word/medical-travel/): Travelling from one country to another to be treated. It is the name this site uses throughout, alongside cross-border care, and the name the trade itself has moved towards over twenty years.
- [Medical visa](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/word/medical-visa/): An entry permission issued for treatment. Some states run a dedicated class that names the hospital and admits a companion; others treat a patient arriving for surgery as an ordinary visitor.
- [Out-of-pocket](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/word/out-of-pocket/): Money a household hands to a provider itself, rather than through a tax, a premium or a pooled fund.
- [Package price](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/word/package-price/): One figure covering a named list of items for one episode of treatment: theatre time, a surgeon, an anaesthetist, a stated number of nights. It is the form almost every price on this site takes.
- [Patient mobility](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/word/patient-mobility/): The European Union's word for patients receiving healthcare in a member state other than the one that insures them, and being reimbursed for it at home.
- [Prior authorisation](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/word/prior-authorisation/): A payer's advance decision that a treatment is medically necessary.
- [Repatriation](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/word/repatriation/): Moving a patient who cannot fly commercially from where they were treated to a hospital at home that can finish the job — or moving a body.
- [Reproductive exile](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/word/reproductive-exile/): Travelling abroad for fertility treatment because it is unlawful, unavailable or unaffordable at home.
- [Revision](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/word/revision/): A second operation on the site of a first: an implant replaced, a nose re-cut, a sleeve converted, a graft redone.
- [Tariff](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/word/tariff/): A schedule of amounts set by a state or an insurer for named items of care. It fixes what the payer will pay, or refund, for each item.
- [Wellness travel](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/word/wellness-travel/): Travel undertaken to maintain or improve wellbeing rather than to treat a condition.

## Data
- [CDC assisted reproductive technology results](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/dataset/cdc-art-results/): What every reporting fertility clinic in the United States did in a year, and what came of it.
- [Current health expenditure per person](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/dataset/world-bank-health-spending/): What a country spends on health in a year, divided by its population, in current US dollars. The World Bank republishes it from the WHO Global Health Expenditure Database.
- [HFEA fertility treatment results](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/dataset/hfea-results/): What every licensed fertility clinic in the United Kingdom did, and what came of it.
- [Hospital beds per 1,000 people](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/dataset/world-bank-beds/): How many hospital beds a country has for every thousand residents.
- [International arrivals](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/dataset/world-bank-tourism-arrivals/): How many international arrivals a country recorded in a year. The World Bank republishes it from UN Tourism's Yearbook and Compendium of Tourism Statistics.
- [Natural Earth country outlines](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/dataset/natural-earth-countries/): The country shapes every map on this site is drawn with. Natural Earth's Admin 0 countries at 1:110 million, fetched once and simplified: 220 country rows, 357 rings, 6,571 coordinate pairs at two decimal places.
- [OECD waiting times for elective surgery](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/dataset/oecd-waiting-times/): How long patients wait for seven non-emergency operations in the countries that measure it. Part of OECD Health Statistics, published with a definitions document dated 10 September 2025.
- [OpenStreetMap hospitals, clinics and dental surgeries](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/dataset/osm-facilities/): Every named hospital, clinic and dental surgery OpenStreetMap carried within a set radius of each hub on this site, fetched through the Overpass API.
- [Out-of-pocket share of health spending](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/dataset/world-bank-out-of-pocket/): What share of a country's health spending comes straight out of households' pockets, rather than from government schemes or insurance.
- [Physicians per 1,000 people](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/dataset/world-bank-doctors/): How many doctors a country has for every thousand residents. The World Bank republishes it from WHO Global Health Workforce Statistics, the OECD and country returns, under a one-line definition: "Physicians include…
- [The dated exchange rate table](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/dataset/exchange-rate-table/): One set of exchange rates, fetched once and stamped, so prices published in twenty-odd currencies can sit on a single axis.
- [The JCI list of accredited organizations](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/dataset/jci-accredited-list/): The directory of hospitals, clinics and programmes outside the United States currently holding Joint Commission International accreditation.
- [WHO Global Health Observatory](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/dataset/who-global-health-observatory/): The World Health Organization's public statistics repository. In its own words, "The GHO data repository is WHO's gateway to health-related statistics for its 194 Member States.

## Stories
- [Circumvention](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/story/circumvention/): Travelling to a country where a treatment is lawful because it is prohibited at home. The act is legal where it happens; the traveller's own state mostly does not reach it.
- [Counting patients](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/story/counting-patients/): Why the headline figures for how many people travel for treatment cannot be added, compared or trusted as counts of people. Twelve of the 52 country records on this site carry an inbound figure.
- [How this was built](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/story/how-this-was-built/): The record shape, the provenance tiers, the price rule, the law rule, the harvests and their licences, the map projection and the editorial rules — set out so that somebody with none of these files could build the same…
- [Is it cheaper](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/story/is-it-cheaper/): One operation, two published prices, worked to the end. A Bangkok hospital's knee package set against an English provider's self-pay list price for the same operation, with the implant, the nights past the package, the…
- [The accreditation question](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/story/the-accreditation-question/): An accreditation is a fact about an inspection somebody bought. The organisation applies, the organisation pays, the survey is scheduled, and the mark runs for a fixed term.
- [The follow-up nobody books](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/story/the-follow-up-nobody-books/): The operation is bought in one country and its consequences are managed in another.
- [The price that isn't](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/story/the-price-that-isnt/): A published price covers a named list of things and excludes another named list, and across 214 price rows on this site the second list is longer than the first 68 times.
- [The queue is the product](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/story/waiting-lists/): Half this directory is about money and the other half is about law, and both miss the commonest reason a person with an insured, funded, free-at-the-point-of-use operation available to them gets on a plane anyway: the…
- [The word itself](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/story/the-word-itself/): This site writes medical travel and cross-border care. The more familiar compound appears only inside a quotation with a speaker attached, inside a proper name, or on the word's own page, where the argument over it is…
- [What the data cannot see](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/story/what-the-data-cannot-see/): Thirteen published series supply every chart, map and table on this site. Each has a record, and each record carries one sentence stating what the series does not count. This page collects those thirteen sentences.
- [Who travels](https://nanobotco.github.io/care-abroad/story/who-travels/): The largest flows anyone counts are not Europeans and North Americans buying cheaper surgery.
